body.statement: In the finite experiment \(\{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}:\theta\in\Gamma_\eta\}\) conditional on \(\mathscr S_\eta\), \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)=\sup_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}Q_{1-\alpha}^{\Pr_{\eta,\theta}}(\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta})\). It is the least member of \(\mathscr C_\eta\) satisfying \(\inf_{\theta\in\Gamma_\eta}\Pr_{\eta,\theta}\{\mathcal L_{\eta,\theta}\leq c(\eta)\}\geq1-\alpha\); no optimality over randomized or observation-dependent radii is claimed. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(G\) and \(R\) with certified Gaussian tail probability at most \(\varepsilon/8\). On \(\mathcal B_{G,R}\), replacing \(\Gamma_\eta\) by \(\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\) preserves the loss, and finite active-set enumeration, interval enclosures for Gaussian rectangle probabilities, grid refinement, and bisection terminate with deterministic brackets for both the worst-case coverage probability and \(c^*(\eta,\alpha)\) of width at most \(\varepsilon\), including structural-zero cases.
body.justification: The theorem gives the exact decision meaning and a terminating certified calculation for the honest local common-cutoff frontier.
body.gap: Andrews--Mikusheva conditional inference and Cox--Shi active-rank testing inform the construction, but neither computes a deterministic common cutoff for a cone-projection plus signed-endpoint loss.
body.consumer: It supplies a finite, auditable oracle benchmark for feasible calibration of the abundance QTE relative to the donor-identified no-intervention law.
